Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Later they adopted the Arab titles sultan and sultān al-salātīn ("Sultan of Sultans").

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: According to the _____ historian known as Munajjim-bashi, a Karakhanid prince named Sultan Satuq Bughra Khan was the first of the khans to convert
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: According to the Ottoman historian called Munajjim-bashi, a Karakhanid prince named Sultan Satuq Bughra Khan was the first of the khans to convert.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211, and the _____ was extinguished by the Khwarazmian Empire in 1212
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Khanate split into the Eastern and Western Khanates in the 1040s. The Eastern Khanate ended in 1211, and the Western Khanate was extinguished by the Khwarazmian Empire in 1212.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: In the late 11th century, they came under the suzerainty of the _____ followed by the Qara Khitai (Western Liao dynasty) who defeated the Seljuks in the Battle of Qatwan in 1141

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Khanate conquered _____ in Central Asia and ruled it independently between 999 and 1089
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Khanate conquered Transoxiana in Central Asia and ruled it independently between 999 and 1089. Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Between 990 and 992, Hasan took _____, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand, and the Samanid capital Bukhara

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Musa (title: _____ or Arslan Khan) resumed the campaign against the Samanids, and by 999 Ali's son Nasr had taken Chach, Samarkand, and Bukhara
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Musa (title: Kara Khan or Arslan Khan) resumed the campaign against the Samanids, and by 999 Ali's son Nasr had taken Chach, Samarkand, and Bukhara.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The Samanid domains were divided between the _____, who gained Khorasan and Afghanistan, and the Karakhanids, who received Transoxiana
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Samanid domains were divided between the Ghaznavids, who gained Khorasan and Afghanistan, and the Karakhanids, who received Transoxiana.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Karakhanid state was divided into appanages (Ülüş system), as was common of Turkic and Mongol nomads.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The dynasty's original domains of _____ and Kasgar and their khans retained an implicit seniority over those who ruled in Transoxiana and Fergana

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Nasr, the conqueror of _____, held the large central area of Transoxiana (Samarkand and Bukhara), Fergana (Uzgen) and other areas, although after his death his appanage was further divided

The dynasty's original domains of Zhetysu and Kasgar and their khans retained an implicit seniority over those who ruled in Transoxiana and Fergana.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Ahmad held _____ and Chach and became the head of the dynasty after the death of Ali

Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Ahmad was succeeded by _____, and after the death of Mansur, the Hasan Bughra Khan branch of the Karakhanids became dominant
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Ahmad was succeeded by Mansur, and after the death of Mansur, the Hasan Bughra Khan branch of the Karakhanids became dominant.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Hasan's sons _____ II, and Yusuf Kadir Khan who held Kashgar, became in turn the head of the Karakhanid dynasty

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The two families, i.e., the descendants of Ali Arslan Khan and Hasan Bughra Khan, would eventually split the _____ in two
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The two families, i.e., the descendants of Ali Arslan Khan and Hasan Bughra Khan, would eventually split the Karakhanid Khanate in two.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: In _____–1018, the Karakhanids repelled an attack by a large mass of nomadic Turkic tribes in what was described in Muslim sources as a great victory
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: In 1017–1018, the Karakhanids repelled an attack by a large mass of nomadic Turkic tribes in what was described in Muslim sources as a great victory.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: In the mid-10th century, Satuq's son Musa began to put pressure on Khotan, and a long period of war between _____ and the Kingdom of Khotan ensued

Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: The "infidels" were said to have been driven towards _____, but the four Imams were killed

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: In 1006, Yusuf Qadir Khan of Kashgar conquered the Kingdom of Khotan, ending Khotan's existence as an independent state.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Eastern Khanate had its capital at Balasaghun and later Kashgar.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: Khidr was returned to power by the Seljuks, but in 1095, the ulama accused Ahmad of heresy and managed to secure his execution.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Liao noble Yelü Dashi recruited warriors from various tribes and formed a horde that moved westward to rebuild the Liao dynasty.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: The Qara Khitai themselves stayed at Zhetysu near Balasagun, and allowed some of the Karakhanids to continue to rule as their tax collectors in Samarkand and Kashgar.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: While the _____ were Buddhists ruling over a largely Muslim population, they were considered fair-minded rulers whose reign was marked by religious tolerance

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Islamic religious life continued uninterrupted and Islamic authority persevered under the _____

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: In _____, the Khwarezm-Shah took Samarkand after the Qara Khitai retreated to deal with the rebellion from the Naiman Kuchlug, who had seized the Qara Khitans' treasury at Uzgen
Kara-Khanid Khanate.fact: In 1210, the Khwarezm-Shah took Samarkand after the Qara Khitai retreated to deal with the rebellion from the Naiman Kuchlug, who had seized the Qara Khitans' treasury at Uzgen.

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Kara-Khanid Khanate.question: Muhammad and _____ had, apparently, agreed to divide up the Qara Khitan's empire

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Kara-Khanid Khanate.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
